summary: When a background pass fails on a stretch of conversation, it now retries with a smaller piece instead of re-sending the same one forever.
details: A pass that fails reads half as much on its next attempt, halving again each time it keeps failing, down to a floor — so a stretch that was slightly too large to handle drains on the first retry rather than never.
A pass that is simply waiting on an unavailable model is unaffected in practice: the smaller attempt succeeds once the model is back, and the next one is full size again.
Operators get a new reading for how often this is happening, so a mis-sized pass is visible instead of looking like an ordinary hourly job.
limitations: The floor means a single stretch that cannot be handled even at the smallest size will still retry indefinitely rather than being set aside.
